title: Bilingual Maths Vocabulary Phone Quiz
whatYouGet: A bilingual maths-term quiz and complete Google Form script that tests meaning in both directions without mistranslating notation.
howToUse: Paste an approved bilingual glossary, review every term pair and example, then run the script and preview both languages on a phone.
effectiveUsage: 1. Supply a trusted glossary or approve the extracted term pairs before quiz generation.
2. Check spelling, register and mathematical meaning with a fluent teacher.
3. Run the script and inspect line wrapping and script rendering on a phone.
4. Use the response summary to separate vocabulary gaps from mathematical misconceptions.
commonFix: If wrong, reply with: "Use only my approved glossary, restore every exact term pair and separate language knowledge from the mathematical answer key."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a bilingual maths-language educator, terminology checker and Google Forms developer.

CONTEXT: A teacher wants students in [CLASS] to connect equivalent maths terms in [LANGUAGE 1] and [LANGUAGE 2] using an approved glossary.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [CLASS]
- [LANGUAGE 1]
- [LANGUAGE 2]
- [APPROVED BILINGUAL GLOSSARY]
- [TOPIC]
- [QUESTION COUNT]
- [SCRIPT OR SPELLING CONVENTION]

DO THIS:
1. Extract only term pairs present in the approved glossary and flag conflicts or missing equivalents for teacher review.
2. Test recognition in both language directions plus meaning-in-context, not transliteration alone.
3. Keep mathematical notation unchanged across languages and use short examples to disambiguate polysemous words.
4. Give a teacher key with a note separating vocabulary errors from maths errors and add check-this-yourself links for numerical examples.
5. Generate one complete executable FormApp script with Unicode text, quiz mode, correct choices, points, feedback and logged URLs.
6. Add a phone typography and language-direction preview checklist.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Build a bilingual vocabulary item around the expression 3*7-2*4.
Expected result or check target: The maths example evaluates to 13 in both languages, while only the approved term labels change.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=3%2A7-2%2A4
(paste-fallback: 3*7-2*4)
Encoding note: The multiplication asterisks and minus signs are URL-safe in this compact query.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. APPROVED TERM INVENTORY
2. BILINGUAL QUIZ REVIEW
3. VOCABULARY-VS-MATHS KEY
4. COMPLETE GOOGLE APPS SCRIPT
5. RUN IT — script.google.com → New project → paste → Run → View → Logs
6. PHONE LANGUAGE PREVIEW

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Use only the teacher’s approved glossary; do not invent translations or silently switch language register.
- Output one COMPLETE executable FormApp code block and print exactly: script.google.com → New project → paste → Run → View → Logs.
- Never translate or alter mathematical symbols, values or formulas.
- Never claim a URL creates the Form; label verification links check this yourself.
- Never describe an AI answer as verified. Every external check must be labelled “check this yourself” for the teacher or student to inspect personally.

title: Forms Results to Re-Teach Priorities
whatYouGet: A question-wise analysis of an exported Google Forms CSV with difficulty, distractor patterns and a ranked re-teach list.
howToUse: Paste a de-identified Forms CSV and checked answer key, confirm the column map, then copy the analysis table and formulas into your working sheet.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a careful assessment-data analyst, answer-key auditor and re-teach planner.

CONTEXT: A teacher has exported [GOOGLE FORMS RESULTS CSV] and needs trustworthy item analysis for [CLASS OR BATCH] without exposing student identities.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [GOOGLE FORMS RESULTS CSV]
- [ANSWER KEY]
- [MARKS SCHEME]
- [QUESTION-TO-TOPIC MAP]

DO THIS:
1. Validate the header row, row count, missing responses and answer-key coverage before calculating anything.
2. Propose an explicit source-column map and stop rather than guessing when two columns are ambiguous.
